tool.modelChoice: Round 1 (layout round): each direction once on Flash and once on Pro so the directions can be compared and the models too. Round 2 and 3 (refinements of the chosen direction): Pro only, as the brief's checklist needs exact strings and a Pip that matches the accepted rich Pip.
tool.output: image/jpeg at 16:9 2K (the size is recorded per call), kept byte-exact in raw/; resampled with LANCZOS to 1536x864 as the canvas PNG; the screen PNG is the detected screen band (or the centred 1024:600 band) resampled to 1024x600.
tool.imageInputs: Sent as inline image parts, each preceded by a short text part stating its role; the preamble, then the prompt verbatim as the last text part.
tool.budget: At most 24 generations across all rounds; 11 used (round 1: 6, round 2: 3, round 3: 2), 3 on gemini-3.1-flash-image and 8 on gemini-3-pro-image. No call failed; none was retried.

directions.A instrument-window: Instrument panel with a large specimen window: the brief's layout as drawn. Vivarium as a bevelled glass window on the left two thirds; a slate bench column of four instrument modules (bay, tray, incubator, Probe dock) on the right third, each a drawn object with an engraved label and a status lamp.
directions.B bench-above: Laboratory bench seen from above at a steep three-quarter angle: the vivarium as a lidless glass terrarium box on a cool slate bench; the bench items standing on the bench as physical instruments; top bar and bottom line as flat chrome strips.
directions.C two-pane: Two-pane readout: the focused resident large (about 340 px) in a deep specimen window on the left 55 percent, the other residents small; a slate instrument readout of the four bench items, drawn larger, on the right 45 percent.

plan.styleGuide: design/style-guide/station-screens.md (Home) arrived on main after round 1 was dispatched; it is the checklist from round 2 on. Differences from brief-home.md are listed in the brief's section 7b: bolt/diamond/drop icons, no wood or felt, cream focus ring, daylight in the vivarium, no lamp-lit bench (which rules direction B out as drawn).
plan.rounds: Round 1: two generations per direction (Flash, Pro). Round 2: refinements of the chosen direction with concrete changes from the critique. Round 3 only if round 2 has a near-pass that one specific change would fix.

calls.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: Miniature Beasts Station HOME screen concept, a flat screen design that fills the whole 16:9 canvas edge to edge (the outer 2 percent at left and right is bleed, trimmed later to 1024x600). Not a device photograph: no bezel, no buttons, no hands, no table. Design at 1024x600 first: large shapes, few words, nothing smaller than 14 px type.
STYLE: the approved Station look: softly sculpted volumes, one key light from the upper left, clean three or four step shading, crisp edges, generous space, no noise, grain or texture spray. The Station is a hardware research instrument, not a room or a cottage. Its chrome is cool and precise: matte dark slate and teal-grey panels, thin engraved rules, small round status lamps, engraved labels, readouts drawn as objects. The vivarium is the only warm, saturated, lively element. Full resolution: smooth volumes and real highlights; pixels may be hinted at the edges but no visible pixel grid.
LAYOUT, as the supplied wireframe: a thin dark top bar (40 px) and a thin dark bottom line (38 px). Between them, on the left two thirds, one large VIVARIUM WINDOW: a glass pane in a bevelled slate frame with a soft edge highlight and small corner ticks. Inside it a lit terrarium: deep moss and teal shadow at the edges, ferns and hanging stems, a small pool, moss along the base. An instrument lamp from the top of the window casts a warm cone onto the focused resident, Pip, sitting on moss at centre, about 300 px tall, exactly the supplied Pip, framed by four thin cream corner brackets. In the shade at the left a small glowtail (a teal, lizard-like mibi with a softly glowing tail tip); at the right a small puffcap (a round mushroom-capped mibi, red cap with cream spots). Lower right of the window a small empty felt bed with a tiny grey Companion-shaped mark on it. On the right third, a vertical slate BENCH COLUMN of four instrument modules, each a drawn object with a small engraved label and one round status lamp at its top right: (1) SAMPLE BAY: a dark hatch holding two sealed wooden crates with small place stamps, one slot empty; (2) POD TRAY: six round cups in a row, three holding smooth seed-pods (one green, one blue, one violet), three empty; (3) INCUBATOR: a glass dome on a plate with a small embryo glowing green inside, and a ring of five leaf shapes around the plate, two of them filled bright; (4) PROBE DOCK: an empty cradle with three small Shield plates beside it, two lit and one dark.
TEXT, exactly these and nothing else, cream type on dark: top bar left "Home  T5"; top bar centre three small icons with counts, an amber energy crystal "9", a blue data chip "4", a green essence droplet "6"; top bar right "Companion away · with Dot". Under the focused resident "Pip" large and "hopper · adult" small. Bottom line: orange "✓ Look at Pip" at left, grey "Pip · hopper · adult" in the middle, grey "a puffcap pod waits · needs 2" with a small green droplet at right.
Constraints: no tables, no panels with title bars, no bullet lists, no digits as timers or counts on the bench, no percentages, graphs, DNA helices, letters for genes or progress bars; no logos or wordmarks; no other creatures than the three residents; no people.
calls.preamble: Reference images follow; their roles are stated. Image 1 is the accepted rich Pip: the focused resident's identity and sculpted treatment (charcoal body, cream belly, orange eyes with cream rings, three green leaf crown lobes, plain coat, three-quarter pose). Image 2 is the approved Station concept: take its light model, cleanliness and clean stepped shading, not its layout or content. Image 3 is the approved flat Station screen: take its header grammar (small icons with counts: blue data chip, amber energy crystal, green essence droplet) and its type colours (cream on dark, amber for a need), not its layout. Image 4 is layout truth only: the boxes and labels show where each element sits at 1024x600; it is not a style reference.

calls.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: Miniature Beasts Station HOME screen concept, 16:9, flat screen design filling the canvas. Edit the supplied screen (Image 1) and preserve everything not named below: the layout, the slate chrome, the top bar and bottom line and all their text, the vivarium's plants, moss, pool and the glowtail, Pip exactly as drawn, the name label. Keep the clean painted light and the crisp edges.
CHANGES, and nothing else: (1) Remove the lamp fixture at the top of the window and its cone; light the vivarium instead with warm daylight falling from the top left, Pip still the brightest thing, a soft cast shadow under it. (2) Replace the four cream corner brackets with one thin warm cream ring resting on the moss around Pip's feet, an ellipse seen in perspective. (3) The red-and-cream mushroom at the right is a creature, a puffcap: give it a small round cream body under the cap, two dark eyes and stubby feet, sitting on the moss. (4) The felt bed becomes a shallow moulded frosted-glass nest with a soft inner glow and a tiny grey Companion-shaped mark inside. (5) In the SAMPLE BAY the two wooden crates become sealed slate-and-teal crates with a small orange seal tag each; the third slot stays empty and dark. (6) The POD TRAY shows exactly six round wells in one row: three with smooth seed-pods (green, blue, violet), three empty; its label reads "Pod rack". (7) The INCUBATOR label reads "Incubation"; keep the dome, the glowing embryo and the five leaves, two bright. (8) The PROBE DOCK shows an empty cradle and, beside it, three small Shield plates as rounded shields, two lit cream and one dark. (9) The top bar icons become a yellow lightning bolt before the 9, a blue diamond before the 4, a green drop before the 6. (10) Each module label is a small engraved readout, not a title bar.
